question: Which white powder, ubiquitous in modern kitchens, combines with acid to produce carbon dioxide?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium bicarbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sodium bicarbonate** is commonly known as **baking soda**.
 
• It is a **chemical compound** with the formula **NaHCO₃**.
 
• When **sodium bicarbonate** reacts with an acid, it produces **carbon dioxide (CO₂) gas**, water, and a salt.
 
• This reaction is utilized in **baking** to help dough rise and become fluffy.
 
• Common acids that react with sodium bicarbonate include **vinegar (acetic acid)** and **lemon juice (citric acid)**.
 
• In addition to baking, sodium bicarbonate is used in **cleaning, deodorizing, and as an antacid** to relieve heartburn and indigestion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sodium phosphate**__

 __
 
• Sodium phosphate is used in various applications including food additives, cleaning agents, and water treatment.
 
 
 
• **Sodium fluoride**__
 __
 
• Sodium fluoride is commonly used in dental products like toothpaste to prevent tooth decay.
 
• It is also used in water fluoridation.
 
 
 
• **Sodium nitrate**__
 
 
• Sodium nitrate is often used as a preservative in cured meats and as a fertilizer.
 
• It is also used in some industrial processes.
